ruling.recommended_action: Close the case; no refund due — the off-route segment was covered by the rider's prior consent and there is no chargeable excess on this fixed-quote RydeX fare.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat (F7–F8), complaint and driver statement contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; no safety dispute type. safety_concern = none.

Route deviation: F3 identifies one off-route segment (10:04–10:11, +2.21 km, up to 1039 m off the optimal route) — an unexplained deviation would breach RD-1 and, for a metered service, attract RD-2. Here the deviation is explained and consented to.

RD-5 consent: the driver proposed the specific route change ("go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1") at 10:01 [F7], before the segment began at 10:04 [F3], and the rider herself replied "Sure, no problem" [F8]. The consent is the rider's own message (not merely the driver's later claim [F10]), and every message is timestamped so there is no completeness gap (G12) [F9]. The scope reading is a specific-route authorisation tied to a named road (Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1), and the recorded segment — narrated by the driver's own chat proposal and shown by GPS — corresponds to that route; nothing places the driven segment on a different road. The segment is therefore exempt, and I need not rely solely on the general "traffic building up" reasoning.

RD-4 not needed, and in any case not satisfied for a stand-alone exemption: the traffic record shows band 2 on Tampines Expressway during 09:48–10:04 [F11] (borderline as RD-4(b) corroboration only) and no incidents at all [F14]; under RD-4(a)/(b) alone the segment would not be exempted.

RD-2 quantum: this is RydeX, a non-metered fixed-quote service, so the fare does not vary with distance travelled [F4, F6]. The only recoverable items would be ERP/tolls actually incurred on an unexempt segment or unpublished post-trip add-ons; none appear — the fare comprises only base, distance, time, platform fee and a 1.0× multiplier [F5, F6]. Recoverable amount = $0.00, so the outcome is no_action; the record of the driver's off-route driving is noted but, being consented, is not a breach.

RD-6: no refund and no RD-1 breach established, and the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17], so no account flag. The rider's clean record [F16] plays no part either way (profile facts never decide a case alone).

segment_findings.reason: RD-5: the driver proposed the named route (Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1) at 10:01 [F7], before the segment started at 10:04 [F3], and the rider's own message agreed [F8]; all messages are timestamped [F9], and the record ties the driven segment to the named road. Consent covers this segment, so it is not part of any unexempt detour under RD-1.

rejected_claims.reason: The +2.21 km off-route segment [F3] is real, but it was a route the rider herself agreed to in advance [F7, F8], so it is exempt under RD-5 and not a breach of RD-1.

Traffic facts do not independently exempt the segment: band 2 on Tampines Expressway [F11] is corroboration only under RD-4(b) and there were no incidents [F14]. The exemption rests on RD-5 consent, not on RD-4.
